mcp.title: Connect an AI app (MCP)
mcp.intro: Claude Desktop, Codex, Antigravity and other MCP clients can design screens through the OpenDGUS MCP server. Add it to the app with the settings below. The project folder is shared, so the AI's changes appear here live.
mcp.devNote: Development build: this points at your Python environment. Installed copies of OpenDGUS show the bundled opendgus-mcp program.
mcp.unavailable: The MCP server location is not known in this mode. Run the desktop app, or see docs/mcp.md.
mcp.claudeHow: Add this to {{path}} (merge it with any existing "mcpServers"), then quit and restart Claude Desktop.
mcp.antigravityHow: Agent panel → … → MCP Servers → Manage → View raw config, then add:
mcp.liveNote: Ask the AI for example: "Create a 800x480 thermostat screen in this project."

settings.title: Project settings
settings.dimHint: The display dims itself (no controller needed) and the next touch only wakes it. It is stored in T5LCFG.CFG, which the display reads from an SD card. After a USB/UART upload it stays active until power-off; the generated controller code switches it on again at every start-up. Longest time: 655 s.
settings.imageHint: A picture or an animated GIF (up to 30 frames), scaled to fill the screen. Every frame is a full-screen image in the display's flash.
settings.saverNeedsController: The display firmware cannot switch pages by itself, so your controller shows and hides the screensaver. The generated code (Arduino, Pico, ESP32, Raspberry Pi) already does it. Without a controller the screensaver page still works as a page: a touch leaves it.

controller.title: Controller code
controller.mqttHint: Publish every variable over MQTT; Home Assistant finds them by itself
controller.intro: OpenDGUS writes the program for the board that drives this display: it receives every touch, writes values to the screen, switches auto-dim on at start-up and runs the screensaver. Choose your board.
controller.baudWarn: The display runs at {{baud}} baud, too fast for this board's display port (max {{max}}).
controller.userCode: Your code between the USER CODE markers is kept when you update.
controller.busy_build: Building (the first time installs the board package, a few minutes)…
controller.uploaded: Uploaded: the board is running the new program
controller.samplesHint: A sample creates a new project: a small design and its controller code, ready to upload.
controller.sampleFolder: Folder for the new sample project
controller.needsNetwork: Needs a board with a network (Pico 2 W, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, PC)
